key_insight: A first-principles multiscale search identifies monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides predicted to host skyrmions, bimerons, and complex magnetic domain states.
engineering_relevance: These candidate materials could support future spin-based devices, while the transferable workflow enables screening of competing magnetic interactions and large-scale spin textures.
method: Compute electronic and magnetic properties using relativistic density functional theory.
Extract microscopic magnetic interactions using magnetic force theory.
Predict emergent spin textures with atomistic spin-dynamics simulations.
evidence_signal: The study computationally screens 312 monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides across 1T and 2H phases containing 3d, 4d, and 5d transition metals.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational predictions, not experimental confirmation of texture stability in fabricated monolayers.
paper_title: First-principles-based search for emergent topological spin textures in transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers
